study_identification_part.si_4_title: Dissecting Heterogeneity in Functional Network Connectivity Aberrations in Antipsychotic Medication-Naïve First Episode Psychosis Patients - A Normative Modeling Study

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Predictive Clinical Neuroscience (PCN) toolkit (version 0.27) used. Specific algorithm (e.g., BLR, GPR) not explicitly stated in the text, but PCN toolkit is specified.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Here, we used the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience (PCN) toolkit (version 0.27), a publicly available Python package, for normative modeling of resting state connectivity data.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Resting-state functional connectivity using the Yeo-17 functional network parcellation atlas, resulting in 136 connectivity values.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Individual-level patterns of deviations from a normative reference range in resting-state functional networks using the Yeo-17 atlas for parcellations. ... resulting in a functional connectivity matrix of 136 connectivity values.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age is implied by 'across the lifespan (age range (yrs): 2-100)'. Site is implied by 'calibration' using local healthy controls.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: The normative model was generated using resting state connectivity data from approximately 22,000 healthy individuals across the lifespan (age range (yrs): 2-100). Healthy control data collected in this project were used for calibration of the normative reference curves
